title: DLA DIBBS spare-parts dealer (approved-source NSN quoting, drop-ship)
product_service: Quoting and fulfilling DLA automated RFQs on DIBBS for National Stock Numbers (bearings, fittings, valves, hardware, electrical, aircraft accessories) by sourcing the approved-source part number from OEMs/authorized distributors and shipping to DLA depots.
target_customer: Defense Logistics Agency supply chains (Land & Maritime, Aviation, Troop Support) buying commercial-like spares for DoD.
purchase_motivation: Readiness: DLA must replenish stock continuously; most buys are automated small purchases awarded on price among acceptable offers.
spending_evidence: DLA FY2025 contract obligations $58.28B, $24.62B to small businesses [A, WS08-S017]; ~6,400 small-business recipients with positive FY2025 DLA obligations; firm ranked ~3,000 received ~$0.18M, ~2,000 ~$0.5M, ~1,000 ~$1.9M [A, WS08-S018]; 206 Illinois small firms received DLA obligations [A, WS08-S019]; DLA SB product POs 288,938 averaging ~$14k [A, WS08-S039]; Fast Auto Evaluation RFQs at/below MPT are not set aside [A, WS08-S033].
representative_operators: Cavanaugh Government Group LLC (IL) - $7.4M DLA FY2025 obligations [A, WS08-S019]
Kampi Components Co - $112.9M on awards <=$350k [A, WS08-S039]
Jamaica Bearings Co - $110.0M on awards <=$350k [A, WS08-S039]
revenue_mechanism: Resale spread: DLA award price minus supplier cost and freight; volume of many small POs.
typical_transaction_value: ~$14k average DLA small-business product PO; many automated awards far below the $15k MPT [A, WS08-S039, WS08-S002]
direct_costs: Part cost from OEM/distributor, freight to depot, packaging/marking to MIL-STD-129/2073, bid-software subscriptions, quality documentation.
contribution_profit_note: E: at ~15-20% gross margin, a $14k average PO contributes ~$2-3k before overhead; quoting win rates unknown (MISSING).
working_capital_note: Supplier typically paid at order or net-30 (credit lines unlikely for a new firm); DLA pays ~30 days after acceptance via WAWF per Prompt Payment rules [A, WS08-S009]; late interest 4.75% (Jul-Dec 2026) [A, WS08-S010]. Revolving float of 30-60 days of purchases.
sales_cycle: Days: RFQs post daily with short return windows; automated awards can issue before return date [A, WS08-S033].
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract-like: same NSNs re-buy periodically; no guaranteed repeat, each buy competed.
customer_accessibility: High mechanical access: any SAM/CAGE-registered small business can quote; no relationship needed; price-driven automated evaluation.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed/unknown: many approved-source OEMs restrict sales to authorized distributors or quote DLA directly; securing distributor pricing as an unknown reseller is the key uncertainty.
competitive_intensity: extreme - thousands of dealers with automated bidding; established 'small' dealers include very large firms (ADS $5.6B) [A, WS08-S018].
entry_strategy: Pick 2-3 FSC niches (e.g., 3110 bearings, 4730 fittings, 5330 gaskets) where you build distributor relationships and quote volume with automated parsing; win on speed, accurate traceability and low quality-defect rate.
licenses: SAM.gov registration with UEI (renew every 365 days) and CAGE code [A, WS08-S031]; Joint Certification Program (DD2345) for export-controlled drawings (MISSING verification); no state license.
regulatory_barriers: Approved-source/traceability rules for non-manufacturers; counterfeit-parts and product-quality deficiency exposure; Buy American/Berry provisions; NMR waived under SAT for SB set-asides [A, WS08-S012].
operational_risks: Wrong-part or non-conforming shipments trigger PQDRs, poor PIPRS scores and eventual exclusion; supplier lead-time misses; packaging non-compliance.
financial_risks: Pricing errors on automated awards; supplier price increases after award; float risk if DLA rejects shipment.
geographic_constraints: None material; ship nationally from suppliers; Illinois location irrelevant.
founder_expertise: FSC/NSN data, DIBBS mechanics, MIL packaging, traceability documentation, supplier negotiation.
staffing: Founder quotes first 6-12 months; then 1-2 bid/quote clerks and a shipping/QA coordinator.
automation_potential: Strong: parsing RFQs, matching NSN-to-supplier P/N, price-history models and auto-quoting; human still needed for supplier relationships, QA and dispute handling.
delegation_potential: Good once SOPs exist: quoting and order administration are clerical/analytical roles.
scalability: Moderate: add FSC niches and quoters; margin pressure and supplier access cap growth; top-1,000 DLA small vendors exceed ~$1.9M obligations [A, WS08-S018].
expansion: Non-DLA federal SAP RFQs (WS08-003), alternate-offer manufacturing (WS08-002), prime-vendor subcontracting, commercial MRO.
roic_note: E: capital mainly working-capital float ($10-25k); if $500k-$1.5M revenue at 15-20% GM, operating profit could be multiples of capital at risk.
critical_assumptions: A new reseller can obtain competitive supplier pricing on approved-source parts
Gross margin 8-30% holds after freight and packaging
Quote win rate sufficient to reach ~$500k revenue by year 2-3
unanswered_questions: Realized dealer gross margins by FSC (no A/B source found)
Share of DIBBS RFQs open to non-manufacturer dealers vs restricted to approved manufacturers
Typical win rates for new CAGE codes
Current DIBBS daily RFQ volume (dla.mil blocked)
failure_modes: Supplier refuses to sell or undercuts by quoting DLA directly
Cash float strain when awards spike
score_rationale: access 7: buyers post RFQs daily and evaluate automatically, no relationships needed [A]. entry 4: extreme price competition. ai 7: RFQ parsing and price modeling are real, durable cost levers. fcf 4: long-tail data shows most small vendors earn <$0.5M revenue/yr [A].
preliminary_verdict: advance - the most open, data-rich federal entry point; economics hinge on unverified dealer margins and supplier access.

title: DLA alternate-offer / reverse-engineered parts via contract manufacturers (SAR route)
product_service: Winning DLA buys for sole-source or limited-source NSNs by getting a Source Approval Request (SAR)/alternate-offer approved and producing parts through partner machine shops.
target_customer: DLA Aviation / Land & Maritime engineering support activities and buying offices.
purchase_motivation: DLA seeks second sources to cut price and lead time on OEM-locked parts.
spending_evidence: DLA Aviation FY24 obligations $8.725B, mostly via DIBBS [A, WS08-S034]; airframe structural components PSC 1560 $243M to small businesses on awards <=$350k in FY2025 [A, WS08-S039].
representative_operators: Kaney Aerospace LLC (IL) - $5.4M DLA FY2025 [A, WS08-S019]
revenue_mechanism: Manufactured-part sales; margin from price below OEM vs outsourced production cost.
direct_costs: Contract machining, materials, first-article testing, inspection, technical data, certifications.
contribution_profit_note: E: higher margins than drop-ship reselling but each approval consumes months of engineering effort.
working_capital_note: Pay shops before DLA acceptance; first articles add months of carry; net-30 after acceptance [A, WS08-S009].
sales_cycle: 6-24 months for approvals (E); then price-competed buys.
repeat_purchase: recurring: approved source status allows repeated quoting on the NSN.
customer_accessibility: Moderate-low: process exists but is engineering-gated.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: Midwest job shops plentiful; willingness to do small defense runs unknown.
competitive_intensity: moderate - fewer competitors than drop-ship NSNs.
entry_strategy: Target NSNs with high price/lead time and available tech data; partner with an AS9100 shop.
licenses: SAM/CAGE; JCP DD2345 for export-controlled data; ITAR registration with DDTC may be required for defense-article manufacturing (MISSING verification) [E].
regulatory_barriers: Technical data rights, first article testing, quality systems, export control.
operational_risks: Failed first articles, shop quality escapes.
financial_risks: Sunk engineering cost on NSNs that never re-buy.
founder_expertise: Engineering drawings, GD&T, quality systems; founder's technical background helps but no mechanical-manufacturing evidence.
automation_potential: AI helps screen NSN buy histories and draft SARs; manufacturing and approvals stay human.
scalability: Moderate, portfolio of approved NSNs compounds.
expansion: Prime subcontract machining, commercial aerospace aftermarket (cross-stream WS03).
roic_note: E: capital tied up in approvals and first articles; returns lumpy.
critical_assumptions: Tech data available for target NSNs
unanswered_questions: Share of buys restricted to approved sources
ITAR registration need for brokered manufacturing
score_rationale: entry 6: approvals form a moat. access/cash low: long engineering-gated cycles and first-article carry.
preliminary_verdict: hold - better as a year-2+ extension of WS08-001 than a starting business.

title: Federal open-market small-business set-aside commodity RFQ reseller (SAM.gov, non-DLA)
subindustry: Commercial products resale to federal agencies
product_service: Responding to SAM.gov combined synopsis/solicitations ($15k-$350k) from Army, Navy, Air Force, VA, NPS, USDA, BOP etc. for brand-name-or-equal commercial items (lab equipment, tools, furniture, electronics, safety gear), sourced from distributors and drop-shipped.
target_customer: Contracting officers at federal installations/field offices buying above the micro-purchase threshold.
purchase_motivation: Buys above $15k and at/below $350k must be set aside for small business when two capable small firms are expected [A, WS08-S003, WS08-S004]; resellers can supply large-business products because NMR does not apply under SAT [A, WS08-S012].
spending_evidence: FY2025 product purchase orders: 596,598 / $11.26B; small businesses 484,129 / $7.48B; explicit SB set-aside 91,034 / $3.08B of which DLA $1.73B (rest Navy $267M, AF $250M, Army $242M, BOP $135M, VA $67M) [A, WS08-S020].
representative_operators: MISSING - long tail of small resellers; not separately identified
typical_transaction_value: ~$15k average small-business product PO; set-aside POs average ~$34k ($3.08B/91k) [A, WS08-S020]
direct_costs: Product cost, freight, bid-matching subscriptions, proposal time.
contribution_profit_note: E: $34k average set-aside PO at ~12-18% GM = ~$4-6k contribution; low win rates on many quotes.
working_capital_note: Pay distributor before or soon after shipment; government pays ~30 days after acceptance/invoice [A, WS08-S009]; card payments for some orders.
repeat_purchase: occasional - each buy re-competed; some agencies set up BPAs with good vendors.
customer_accessibility: Moderate: public RFQs reachable by anyone registered; evaluation often lowest-price technically acceptable.
supplier_accessibility: Unknown: distributors may refuse reseller pricing or bid directly; brand-name restrictions.
competitive_intensity: high - many bid shops; RFO/EO 14240 push agencies to GSA schedules and consolidated vehicles [C, WS08-S005; A, WS08-S032].
entry_strategy: Specialize in 2-3 categories where specs are technical (founder's research background, e.g., lab/scientific equipment) to win on technical acceptability and speed.
licenses: SAM registration/UEI [A, WS08-S031]; no state license.
regulatory_barriers: Buy American / TAA representations; limitations on subcontracting/NMR above SAT [A, WS08-S012].
operational_risks: Spec mismatches, shipment delays, unclear brand-name-or-equal judgments.
financial_risks: Low margins leave little room for freight surprises; agency budget freezes.
founder_expertise: FAR basics, quoting, product specs, compliance reps & certs.
automation_potential: AI triage of SAM.gov notices, spec matching, draft quotes; humans for supplier negotiations.
scalability: Moderate; policy trend toward schedule/BIC consolidation may shrink open-market share.
roic_note: E: very low capital; returns depend on founder/analyst time.
critical_assumptions: Open-market SAP set-asides persist despite consolidation
Distributors will quote a new reseller
unanswered_questions: Effect of EO 14240 consolidation on FY2026 open-market POs
failure_modes: Consolidation to GSA vehicles removes open-market RFQs
score_rationale: Strong statutory reservation for small business [A] and large public spend [A], but consolidation policy risk lowers resilience; margins unverified.
preliminary_verdict: advance - pair with WS08-001 as one federal SAP reseller operation.

title: Local federal installation micro-purchase (GPC card) supplier in Illinois
product_service: Same-week supply of MRO, lab, IT accessories and facility consumables to cardholders at Naval Station Great Lakes, Scott AFB, Rock Island Arsenal, VA medical centers (Hines, Jesse Brown, Lovell FHCC) and other Illinois federal sites, paid by government purchase card under $15k.
target_customer: Government purchase cardholders (maintenance shops, labs, admin offices) at Illinois federal facilities.
purchase_motivation: Micro-purchases need no formal competition up to $15k [A, WS08-S002]; cardholders value speed and local delivery.
spending_evidence: Illinois-performed FY2025 federal contracts: 699,752 awards; DLA $3.56B, Army $1.97B, VA $1.68B, Air Force $1.16B, Navy $621M [A, WS08-S021]. Card micro-purchases are not individually reported to FPDS, so local card spend is MISSING [A, WS08-S008].
representative_operators: MISSING - card vendors not visible in FPDS
typical_transaction_value: <=$15,000 per card transaction (often much smaller) [A for limit, WS08-S002; value distribution MISSING]
direct_costs: Product cost, card processing fees (~2-3%, E), local delivery.
working_capital_note: Card pays at charge/shipment - fast cash; inventory if stocking.
sales_cycle: Days once known; months to get known.
repeat_purchase: recurring if a cardholder adopts you.
acquisition_channels: Direct outreach (not allowed for this research phase)
customer_accessibility: Low-moderate: base access controls; cardholders steered to mandatory sources (AbilityOne, FedMall/GSA) first.
competitive_intensity: high - Grainger, Amazon Business, GSA Advantage are default choices.
entry_strategy: Hyper-local fast delivery of hard-to-find items for maintenance/lab shops.
regulatory_barriers: Required-sources priority; equitable distribution of micro-purchases.
geographic_constraints: Chicago north suburbs, Metro East (Scott AFB), Quad Cities - dispersed.
founder_expertise: Base procurement culture, local supplier network.
scalability: Low: limited cardholder base in IL; can't verify spend.
expansion: Feeds WS08-003 set-aside RFQs and BPAs.
roic_note: E: low capital; low absolute profit.
critical_assumptions: Cardholders will buy from an unknown local vendor
score_rationale: Fast card cash (cash 7) but small, invisible demand and channel defaults (access 4, scale 3).
preliminary_verdict: hold - useful feeder channel, not a standalone business.

title: Bureau of Prisons food-service commodity bid supplier
product_service: Winning BOP institution food purchase orders (oils/fats/shelf-stable, meat, dairy, bakery, produce) by brokering manufacturer/distributor truckloads delivered to prison docks.
target_customer: Food-service administrators/contracting staff at federal correctional institutions (Illinois: FCI Pekin, FCI Greenville, USP Marion, AUSP Thomson, MCC Chicago; ~120 nationally - count unverified).
purchase_motivation: Mandatory inmate feeding; buys competed via small-business set-aside POs.
spending_evidence: BOP FY2025 small-business product POs: 5,761 / ~$155M; food PSCs: 8945 $64.2M, 8905 $29.3M, 8910 $11.9M, 8915 $10.5M, 8920 $8.2M; Illinois-performed 175 POs / $3.57M [A, WS08-S023]; BOP total product SB set-aside POs $135M [A, WS08-S020].
representative_operators: Advanced Commodities, Inc. - $2.75M of IL BOP POs FY2025 [A, WS08-S023]
revenue_mechanism: Resale spread per PO; volume across institutions.
typical_transaction_value: ~$27k average BOP SB product PO [A, WS08-S023]
contribution_profit_note: Incumbent food-distribution economics: Sysco FY2026 GM 18.5%, op margin 3.7% [A, WS08-S037 - incumbent economics]; a broker likely earns 5-12% GM (E).
working_capital_note: Perishables paid within ~7-10 days under Prompt Payment rules [A, WS08-S009]; shelf-stable net-30; supplier terms for a new broker MISSING.
customer_accessibility: Moderate: public, price-based bids; national footprint reachable.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: food manufacturers/distributors sell to brokers; kosher/halal/religious-diet items specialized.
entry_strategy: Focus on specialty/religious-diet and shelf-stable lines with nationwide delivery; reliable on-time delivery records.
licenses: SAM registration; FDA food facility registration only if warehousing (MISSING verification) [E].
regulatory_barriers: Food specs, Buy American, delivery windows into secure facilities.
financial_risks: Commodity price swings between bid and delivery.
automation_potential: Bid tracking, price modeling; logistics remain human.
expansion: Other institutional feeding (VA, state DOC, county jails - judge carefully).
roic_note: E: modest working capital; thin margins.
unanswered_questions: Number of bidders per BOP food PO
score_rationale: Durable mandated demand and public bids (access 6, resilience 7) but distributor-thin margins [A incumbent] cap fcf.
preliminary_verdict: hold - credible niche of the federal SAP reseller cluster; verify margins and bidder counts.

title: GSA Multiple Award Schedule product reseller (Startup Springboard entry)
product_service: Holding a GSA MAS contract (e.g., industrial products, scientific equipment, facilities SINs) listing resold commercial products on GSA Advantage/eBuy for agency orders.
target_customer: Federal (and some state/local via cooperative purchasing for IT/disaster SINs) ordering offices.
purchase_motivation: Policy prioritizes schedules/GWACs/BICs [C, WS08-S005]; EO 14240 consolidates common-goods buying into GSA [A, WS08-S032]; FY2026 NDAA Sec. 812 lets DoD place MAS orders on best value [C, WS08-S006].
spending_evidence: MAS annual sales volume MISSING (not retrieved); GSA FAS obligations performed in Illinois $472M FY2025 [A, WS08-S021].
revenue_mechanism: Resale spread on schedule orders minus Industrial Funding Fee [A, WS08-S030].
direct_costs: Product cost, IFF (rate set by FAS, MISSING %) [A, WS08-S030], compliance (TAA, price reductions), consultant fees if used.
contribution_profit_note: E: price-reduction and most-favored-customer mechanics compress margin.
working_capital_note: Net-30 government payment [A, WS08-S009]; product float.
sales_cycle: Offer evaluation months (MISSING exact); then orders require separate marketing.
customer_accessibility: Low-moderate: a schedule is a hunting license, not demand.
supplier_accessibility: Requires letters of supply from manufacturers and TAA-compliant products.
entry_strategy: Apply via Startup Springboard after ~6-12 months of commercial/federal sales in a niche [A, WS08-S029].
licenses: SAM registration; MAS offer requires 2 years corporate experience unless Startup Springboard (FASt Lane-qualified) [A, WS08-S029].
regulatory_barriers: TAA country-of-origin, Commercial Sales Practices disclosure, sales reporting.
financial_risks: IFF and audit exposure; zero sales risk.
roic_note: E: low cash, high time cost before revenue.
critical_assumptions: Springboard offer accepted for a newcomer
score_rationale: Policy tailwind (resilience 7) but schedule != demand; slow (access 4).
preliminary_verdict: hold - a year-2 add-on to an operating federal reseller, not an entry.

title: Federal SAP-level research/data/IT services contractor
product_service: Small-dollar analytic, data, survey, software or research support tasks for federal agencies and DOE labs, priced under the SAT.
target_customer: Program offices at federal agencies; research-heavy buyers.
purchase_motivation: Short-term capacity needs; service POs set aside for small business.
spending_evidence: FY2025 service purchase orders set aside for small business: 22,202 / $0.97B [A, WS08-S020].
typical_transaction_value: ~$43k average SB set-aside service PO ($965M/22,202) [A, WS08-S020]
contribution_profit_note: E: labor-margin business; capped by billable hours.
working_capital_note: Payroll before net-30 federal payment [A, WS08-S009].
sales_cycle: 1-6 months; past performance weighs heavily (DoD guidance on alternative past performance due Dec 2026 [C, WS08-S006]).
customer_accessibility: Low: relationships and past performance dominate.
entry_strategy: Narrow technical niche from founder's research background.
licenses: SAM registration; possible facility/personnel clearances for some work.
regulatory_barriers: Past-performance evaluation, organizational conflict of interest rules.
financial_risks: Federal consulting budget cuts (policy risk, not quantified here).
founder_expertise: Matches founder background, but federal selling skills needed.
automation_potential: AI raises analyst productivity but buyers pay for outputs/hours.
roic_note: High ROIC on little capital but founder-hours-limited.
critical_assumptions: Founder can win first task without past performance
score_rationale: Founder-hour capped and credibility-gated; mandate disfavors pure consulting.
preliminary_verdict: reject - founder-hour consulting with high credibility walls.

title: Tier-2 small-business subcontractor/supplier to federal primes
product_service: Supplying commercial parts, consumables, or services to large primes that need small-business subcontracting credit.
target_customer: Supplier-diversity / purchasing departments of large federal primes and facility-operations contractors.
purchase_motivation: Primes above $900k ($2M construction) must file small-business subcontracting plans [A, WS08-S014].
spending_evidence: Reported first-tier subawards in Illinois are concentrated in large defense suppliers (Chemring $104.6M, Hamilton Sundstrand $20.4M, CDW Government $12.1M) [A, WS08-S038].
representative_operators: CDW Government LLC - $12.1M IL subawards FY2025 [A, WS08-S038]
working_capital_note: Primes typically pay net-45-60 (E); not covered by federal Prompt Payment Act protections in the same way.
entry_strategy: Specialty items the prime's existing distributors don't stock.
critical_assumptions: Primes will onboard a new micro-supplier
preliminary_verdict: hold - opportunistic adjunct, not an entry.
